items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Along the Johnny Hudgins type of a singer.

ctx.x: Well, you see, there was the big wagon that'd pull up -- in the back of the wagon they let the tail down and set up curtains in the back, you know, draped the back with curtains and they'd have a comedian. Now these comedians most of them were very good comedians, and dancers, and joke tellers. And they sang a lot. Along the Johnny Hudgins type of a singer. Course, it wasn't pantomine, but they did -- had some of the best comedians, back in those days on medicine shows. It was a very good job.

And then, of course, the guys that were selling the medicine, naturally, he was white. A very good talker. Very good talker, he would sell his product. I remember one time they had a -- they were selling some kind of a glass that was made out of peppermint of some kind. This glass. And they would sell this glass, I guess maybe 50¢ or something 25¢ or 50¢, it was supposed to cure a lot of things and you poured water in it and then the water would, you know, take the taste of peppermint. From the glass. And it was…
